report.summary: Checkout-service memory usage increased from 697.53 MiB to 1220.35 MiB (1.7×), triggering frequent GC overhead warnings and OutOfMemoryError exceptions.

likely_causes.title: Java heap exhaustion due to insufficient heap size or memory leak
likely_causes.rationale: The service consistently reached 92 % heap usage and threw OutOfMemoryError, indicating the allocated heap is insufficient for the workload or a leak is present.

supporting_evidence.detail: WARN checkout-service: GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92%
ERROR checkout-service: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space

likely_causes.title: Memory leak in application code
likely_causes.rationale: Repeated GC overhead warnings and OOM errors over a short period suggest objects are not being released, pointing to a memory leak.

supporting_evidence.detail: WARN checkout-service: GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92%
ERROR checkout-service: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space

likely_causes.title: External load increase causing higher memory usage
likely_causes.rationale: The 1.7× rise in resident memory aligns with a sudden spike in traffic or transaction volume.

next_steps: Increase the JVM heap size or adjust GC settings to accommodate higher memory demand.
Run a heap profiler (e.g., VisualVM, JProfiler) to identify objects retaining memory and pinpoint leaks.
Analyze traffic patterns and load metrics to confirm whether the memory spike correlates with increased request volume.

detail: Java heap exhaustion due to insufficient heap size or memory leak
